Since symplectic geometry has its origins in classical mechanics, and since integrable systems are essentially physical systems with many conserved quantities, it is natural to ask if considering the same system with coefficients in $\mathbb{R}$ and $\mathbb{Q}_p$ respectively, will lead us to see the same or different behaviors. Our first goal in this paper is prove that the $p$-adic and real local normal forms of the same system have no relation, that is, any combination of real and $p$-adic local normal forms is possible. This implies that $\mathbb{R}$ and $\mathbb{Q}_p$ capture fundamentally different information about the system, despite the fact that they both contain $\mathbb{Q}$ as a dense subset and that experiments can only measure rational quantities. Hence a $p$-adic version of symplectic geometry and Hamiltonian mechanics will be different from its real counterpart, at least from the point of view of integrable systems. Our second goal in this paper is to introduce techniques to compute these normal forms. We establish these results combining Galois theory of $p$-adic fields with analytic estimates.
item.dc:creator: Luis Crespo, \'Alvaro Pelayo

item.title: Genus-One Rigidity of Bounded Virasoro Pairings for 3D Gravity
item.description: arXiv:2608.03459v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study whether varying the topological boundary of the doubled Virasoro TQFT can produce distinct torus pairings for an ensemble interpretation of 3D gravity. In the ordinary nondegenerate sector, every bounded pairing that commutes with the modular transformations is scalar, and vacuum normalization selects the diagonal pairing. The proof identifies the modular transformations with the even Weil representation and applies the Cowling--Steger lattice-restriction theorem. Under the ordinary block-diagonal vacuum--continuum ansatz, positivity and the two vacuum marginals also make a Borel-measure pairing bounded, without assuming absolute continuity; modular invariance then forces the same diagonal pairing. These two classes therefore contain no distinct torus pairings to average. A nontrivial Virasoro boundary ensemble must involve genus-one data outside these classes, additional sectors or vacuum--continuum couplings, or information invisible in the torus pairing. Elementary proofs in explicit regular sectors explain the rigidity mechanisms, and numerical calculations provide independent checks.
item.dc:creator: Xingyang Yu

item.title: A globally defined compressible polyconvex isotropic energy satisfying the true-stress-true-strain monotonicity condition (TSTS-M++)
item.description: arXiv:2609.06026v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct a compressible isotropic energy on $\mathrm{GL}^+(3)$ combining polyconvexity and global true-stress-true-strain monotonicity (TSTS-M++), answering a question of Wollner, Holzapfel and Neff. For every $\mu>0$ and $k>0$, the energy $W_k(F)=\frac{\mu}{2k}[\exp(k(\lVert F\rVert^2+3J^{-1}+J-7))-1]$, $J=\det F$, is polyconvex and strictly rank-one convex. Its Cauchy-stress response satisfies TSTS-M++ globally if and only if $k\ge1/(8\sqrt3)$. The reference state is stress free with positive infinitesimal shear and bulk moduli. Stress bijectivity has the smaller sharp threshold $k_{\rm B}\approx0.0083$: at equality the stress map is a global homeomorphism with a nondifferentiable inverse, and above it a global smooth diffeomorphism. Thus, for $k_{\rm B}\le k<1/(8\sqrt3)$, the Cauchy-stress map remains globally bijective while TSTS-M++ fails at finite strain. In the TSTS-M++ regime, each prescribed inner radius of a finite plane-strain annulus with a traction-free outer wall has a unique radial equilibrium, and the inner pressure increases smoothly and strictly from zero to infinity. Comparisons with other energies distinguish the roles of polyconvexity, TSTS-M++, reduced convexity and endpoint growth. Under incompressible spherical inflation, global pressure inversion holds for the Demiray family with $b\ge b_*$, including $W_k|_{J=1}$ for $k\ge k_*$ and the stress-free $I_1$-exponential energy, and for the exponentiated Hencky energy when $k_{\mathrm{eH}}>3/8$. Incompressible neo-Hooke instead has a limit point. A further compressible $I_1$ energy retains the global constitutive properties and reference moduli of $W_k$ but exhibits two pressure turning points under incompressible spherical inflation, showing that these properties allow a descending pressure branch.
item.dc:creator: Dongxin Bai, Yunhao Wu, Yong Li, Kai Zhang, Patrizio Neff

item.title: Modified scattering for semiclassical Bose-Fermi mixtures
item.description: arXiv:2609.06143v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Vlasov-Hartree system models a mixture of bosons and fermions interacting via Coulomb forces in which the bosons are described quantum-mechanically, while the fermions are described classically. For small initial data, we prove that the system exhibits modified scattering, i.e. the bosonic and fermionic subsystems each converge to solutions of the free Schr\"odinger and Vlasov equations respectively, but with coupled logarithmic corrections owing to the long-range nature of Coulomb interactions. We use a mixed Lagrangian and Fourier-based approach to derive explicit descriptions of the asymptotic dynamics of the solution and associated fields and Lagrangian trajectories. Notably, due to our purely Lagrangian analysis on the Vlasov side, we require no derivatives on the initial fermion density, the asymptotic fermionic profile is as regular as the initial data, and convergence occurs in almost the same space as the initial data.
item.dc:creator: Kieran Cavanagh

item.title: Regularized barycentric R\'enyi divergences
item.description: arXiv:2609.17517v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Barycentric R\'enyi divergences were introduced in [Mosonyi, Bunth, Vrana, Linear Algebra and its Applications, 2024] as an alternative to standard Kubo-Ando constructions to define multivariate quantum R\'enyi divergences. They are defined via a variational expression and depend on a finite collection of quantum relative entropies $D^{q_x}$. When all the relative entropies are monotone under CPTP maps then so are the corresponding barycentric R\'enyi divergences, and when all the relative entropies are additive then the corresponding barycentric R\'enyi divergences are subadditive under tensor product. Additivity has only been established before for the case where all $D^{q_x}$ are chosen to be the Umegaki relative entropy, which is also the only case where the barycentric R\'enyi divergence (called the minimal one) was known to admit an explicit expression. Here we settle the problem of additivity by showing that for any choice of monotone quantum relative entropies, the regularized barycentric R\'enyi divergence coincides with the minimal barycentric R\'enyi divergence on invertible inputs. This in turn implies that if at least two of the $D^{q_x}$ are strictly larger than the Umegaki relative entropy (in a precise sense), then the resulting barycentric R\'enyi divergence is not even weakly additive.
item.dc:creator: Mil\'an Mosonyi

item.title: Spectral Numbers in Tate Rabinowitz Floer Homology
item.description: arXiv:2609.39951v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that circle-valued spectral values in Tate Rabinowitz Floer homology give rise to quantized energy levels, which recover the quantum mechanical spectrum of a system of uncoupled harmonic oscillators.
item.dc:creator: Kai Cieliebak, Urs Frauenfelder

item.title: The quantum-classical bipartite universe and the logical emergence of $\hbar$ from classical temporality
item.description: arXiv:2610.05083v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a foundational reinterpretation of quantum dynamics based on the standard von Neumann formalism, positing a structural logical bipartition between a classical observational environment and a quantum observed system. Against universalist frameworks, we argue that theoretical consistency requires distinct propositional logics: Boolean logic governs the environment, while non-Boolean logic applies to the observed system. Within this framework, an ideal classical clock is represented as an open system whose energy spectrum is uniformly discretized. The dynamics follow from the Gorini-Kossakowski-Sudarshan-Lindblad (GKSL) master equation under the constraint that the Hamiltonian remains observable. Although the clock's temporal evolution is driven by dissipative coupling to the measurement apparatus, it admits a deterministic solution corresponding to information-preserving cyclic dynamics. This deterministic regime may emerge as a logical attractor, stabilized by the Boolean structure inherent to the measurement interaction. Ultimately, $\hbar$ is derived as a fundamental scaling parameter from the classical clock's action operator, revealing that the quantum of action reflects the discrete logical structure underlying classical temporality. Furthermore, this framework establishes an exact mapping with 't Hooft's cellular automaton formalism, offering an alternative ontological interpretation that not require hidden variables and superdeterministic assumptions. The resulting distinction between quantum dynamics (as potential recontextualization) and classical dynamics (as temporal actualization) provides a novel logical approach to the measurement problem.
item.dc:creator: Vincenzo Chilla

item.title: The $L^1$-realization of an elliptic operator with unbounded coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2610.06659v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish an $L^1$-theory for a class of elliptic operators with unbounded coefficients, extending our earlier semigroup generation results and those of Canale--Rhandi--Tacelli to the endpoint $p=1$. The $L^1$-realization generates a positive analytic $C_0$-semigroup that is compact for every positive time. We characterize the generator domain through weighted estimates and prove consistency with the corresponding $L^p$-semigroups for $1<p<\infty$.
item.dc:creator: Sallah Eddine Boutiah

item.title: Energy-constrained two-way capacities of pure-loss and quantum-limited amplifier channels
item.description: arXiv:2610.06832v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We determine the two-way quantum, entanglement-distribution, private, and secret-key capacities of the pure-loss bosonic channel under an unconditional mean transmitted-photon-number constraint. For transmissivity $\eta$ and mean photon number $N$, all four capacities coincide and are given by $g(N)-g((1-\eta)N)$, where $g$ is the entropy of a thermal mode. This resolves the longstanding energy-constrained capacity problem by establishing the optimality of the reverse-coherent-information rate introduced in 2009. Our central tool is sector teleportation simulation, which we develop specifically to transfer the input-energy constraint to the shared entanglement resource, thereby preserving the constraint throughout converse arguments for general adaptive protocols. For every $N>0$, we further show that the corresponding strong-converse thresholds coincide with the unconstrained value $-\log_2(1-\eta)$. For parallel protocols with a hard total-photon-number cutoff, the same energy-constrained capacity formula instead satisfies an exponential strong converse. As an extension, we determine the energy-constrained two-way capacities of the quantum-limited amplifier, showing that classical assistance does not improve its unassisted quantum and private rates. Together, these results establish a unified finite-energy framework for adaptive bosonic communication and reveal how energy constraints fundamentally reshape both attainable rates and converse bounds.
item.dc:creator: Stefano Pirandola

item.title: Energy-constrained two-way capacity bounds for noisy Gaussian channels
item.description: arXiv:2610.08786v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A gap between achievable rates and converse bounds persists for energy-constrained bosonic communication in the presence of excess noise. We derive a unified adaptive weak-converse bound for thermal attenuation, noisy amplification, and additive Gaussian noise under an unconditional mean transmitted-photon-number constraint. The bound applies to arbitrary adaptive protocols with quantum memories and constrains the two-way quantum, entanglement-distribution, private, and secret-key capacities. It vanishes throughout the entanglement-breaking region and approaches the corresponding PLOB bound at infinite energy. At finite energy, it improves the evaluated Gaussian squashed-entanglement and PLOB bounds in relevant parameter regimes, while comparison with hashing rates quantifies the remaining gap to achievability. The result provides a common energy-dependent benchmark for noisy bosonic Gaussian channels and extends finite-energy converse methods beyond the quantum-limited setting.
item.dc:creator: Stefano Pirandola

item.title: Haagerup conformal field theory at central charge eight
item.description: arXiv:2610.14441v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct a chiral algebra $U$ of central charge eight inside the lattice vertex operator algebra $V_{E_6\oplus A_2}$. It is generated by two commuting affine $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ current algebras at levels $1$ and $39$, the stress tensor of the lattice theory, and a single weight-two field built from three lattice exponentials. We announce that $U$ is strongly rational and completely unitary, and that $Rep(U)$ is equivalent, as a unitary ribbon category, to the Drinfeld center $Z(\mathcal{H}_3)$ of the Haagerup fusion category $\mathcal{H}_3$. Its characters are the $\gamma=0$ Evans--Gannon vector. From $U$ we obtain a diagonal full CFT, and also a holomorphic $E_8$ extension on which $\mathcal{H}_3$ acts by topological defects.
item.dc:creator: Tzu-Chen Huang

item.title: Harmonic Reduction of Spin-Coupled Grover Walks on Hypercubes via Quantum Bernoulli Noises
item.description: arXiv:2610.14467v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider spin-coupled Grover walks on hypercubes within the framework of quantum Bernoulli noises (QBN). We identify parity-dependent harmonic subspaces generated by the central Hamming layers: in even dimension they give a fixed-point subspace, whereas in odd dimension the walk reduces on the harmonic subspace to an explicit eight-dimensional reduced dynamics. Using symmetric-group representation theory, we characterize the corresponding isotypic structure and determine the reduced spectrum. The harmonic reduction also yields explicit long-time probability behavior and shows that the resulting states may occupy an asymptotically vanishing fraction of the hypercube while still spanning its full Hamming diameter.
item.dc:creator: Ce Wang
